answer: Weather agents rent posts along a windy ridge and log when gusts pass. Each gust is a pulse of pressure that reaches the posts in an order set by where they truly stand, and that order flips whenever the wind turns. One machine posing as twenty posts never feels the air, so it can only guess the sequence. Copying a real neighbour fails too: two posts a meadow of yarrow apart would report the same instant, though the gust reached them seconds apart.
